To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human ankle muscles use series elasticity in their tendons to produce mechanical work and accelerate during walking.
human ankle muscles use elastic tendons to produce acceleration during gait by transitioning active muscle shortening to series elastic tissue stretch early in the stance.

(1) human ankle muscles with elastic tendons are capable of producing net positive work during walking acceleration; (2) this is accomplished through the reorientation of the leg to keep the muscle isometric while the fascicles actively shorten, stretching the series elastic tissue for subsequent recoil; (3) this is fundamentally different than constant-speed walking, during which ankle muscles with elastic tendon undergo a period of net negative work to store elastic energy before subsequent recoil.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanical behaviour of the human soleus muscle during walking.
the mechanical function of the human ankle muscles during walking and how this function is modulated to produce acceleration.

the role of muscle and tendon in the production of mechanical work during human walking gait, and the integration of these muscle–tendon behaviours with whole-body mechanics to produce accelerative gait.
